result.title: DiRGeo: Learning Directional Geometry of Visual Representations
result.summary: Conventional geometric measures of visual representations are symmetric, assigning equal costs to forward and reverse motion along the same path. We propose DiRGeo, a framework for learning directional geometry over frozen visual representations. Grounded in Randers geometry, DiRGeo learns a state-dependent directional field from ordered image trajectories through self-supervised contrast, without semantic labels. Sphere-tangent correction and attractor-relative decomposition distinguish learned directional structure from normalization artifacts and common convergence. Experiments across 17 visual processes, three encoder families, and multiple representation depths demonstrate consistent directional discrimination and whole-path asymmetry beyond simple attractor-based explanations. The learned fields become increasingly process-specific in deeper representations, while natural-video experiments reveal event-dependent directional preferences. As functional validation, DiRGeo guides restoration selection. These results establish directional geometry as a useful complement to symmetric representation analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DiRGeo，基于 Randers 几何在冻结视觉表征上学一个状态依赖的方向场，用有序图像轨迹做自监督对比，从而给出打破对称性、能区分正反向的表征几何度量，并在多编码器、多深度与视频事件上检验其方向偏好。
AI.relevance_reason: 其非对称、路径级的方向几何可为 LVR 中 latent 相似度分析提供线索：用于核查「先看后想」与「先想后看」等有序状态转移的不可交换性，以及该结构随表征深度的变化，但与原论文主线无直接重叠，需核查迁移可行性。
